title: Stacking Spectra in Protoplanetary Disks: Detecting Intensity Profiles from Hidden Molecular Lines in HD 163296
question: Can aligning spectra by Keplerian velocity before stacking boost S/N of molecular lines in a disk and reveal undetected weak lines and their intensity profiles?

data.sensitivity: 2.4 mJy/beam (DCO+, DCN), 2 mJy/beam (H2CO), 2.9 mJy/beam (N2D+) per channel

external_data.citation: Mannings & Sargent 1997; Isella et al. 2007; Hughes et al. 2008; de Gregorio-Monsalvo et al. 2013; Mathews et al. 2013; Rosenfeld et al. 2013

evidence.quote: Inclination and position angle are measured to be $\sim$45$\ensuremath{^\circ}$ and $\sim$130$\ensuremath{^\circ}$ (Isella et al. 2007).

what.value: Intrinsic line width ΔV_int ~(0.1–0.3)(r/100AU)^q km/s, q from -0.3 to -0.1

evidence.quote: where $q$ ranges from $-0.3$ to $-0.1$ (e.g., Piétu et al. 2007).

recipe.method: Calibrate and CLEAN archival data with natural weighting at 0.1 km/s

recipe.goal: Align and stack spectra by Keplerian velocity
recipe.method: Deproject pixels, compute projected Vk, shift each spectrum by Vk, mirror across minor axis, and sum over radial/azimuthal bins
key_parameters: Radial ranges R<300 AU (DCO+, H2CO), R<200 AU (DCN), 100<R<300 AU (N2D+)

recipe.goal: Derive radial intensity profiles and compare three methods
recipe.method: Radial bins of half beam; mean integrated intensity from moment 0, unaligned stacks, and aligned stacks; uncertainties sigma_a*dv*sqrt(N)
Sectors 1.5 beam radially and 45 deg azimuthally for r>0.45''; inner region averaged over 2π

evidence.quote: are measured to be 12.9$\pm$0.1 and 4.9$\pm$0.1 mJy Beam$^{-1}$ km s$^{-1}$
are measured to be 12.9$\pm$0.1 and 4.9$\pm$0.1 mJy Beam$^{-1}$ km s$^{-1}$

Peak intensity increase for DCO+ and H2CO

evidence.quote: the peak intensities of the spectra increase by a factor $\sim$5

answer_key.quantity: S/N gain of profiles vs moment 0 (DCO+, DCN)

evidence.quote: $\sim$4–6 times higher than those from moment 0 maps
